key_insight: RGB-D segmentation models become unreliable when one modality disappears at test time, even if the remaining modality still contains useful signal. Condition Dropout (ConD) improves robustness by training the model to handle missing RGB or depth during continued training.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the real-world failure mode where RGB or depth sensors are missing, occluded, or malfunctioning, causing standard RGB-D semantic segmentation models to degrade sharply because they were trained only on complete two-modality inputs.
method: Continued-training paradigm: start from a full-modality RGB-D segmentation model and further train it under missing-modality conditions.
Condition Dropout (ConD): randomly drop RGB or depth during training so the network learns to rely on whichever modality remains available.
Robust fusion learning: encourage the model to preserve segmentation performance in both full-input and single-modality scenarios.
impact: This makes RGB-D segmentation more dependable in real deployments such as surveillance, robotics, and autonomous systems where sensor dropouts are common. For practitioners, it offers a simple training-time fix that can improve robustness without redesigning the whole model.

paper_title: Toward Reliable RGB-D Semantic Segmentation: Handling Missing Modalities via Condition Dropout
paper_authors: Xuchen Zhu, Yajuan Wei, Shuang Hao, Jiwei Jiang, Guanxiang Mao
